content.text: {"grade": 6, "complete": false, "main_gap": "Step 2 uses a false principle ('a positive integer that never increases and starts above 1 can never reach 1') to show some entry >1 survives; the correct reason (a move cannot create two 1's) appears only in the summary.", "errors": [{"description": "Step 2's justification is a non-sequitur: a non-increasing positive integer certainly can reach 1 (e.g. 4\u21922\u21921). The needed argument is that a move on m,n>1 yields g\u00b7\u2113 = mn \u2265 4, so it cannot produce two 1's; hence the count of entries >1 never drops to 0. This correct reasoning is stated in the 'Current best' summary but omitted from the 'Full proof'.", "quote": "A positive integer that never increases and starts above $1$ can never reach $1$; hence\n$P > 1$ after any number of moves."}], "notes": "Termination bound (type A halves P, at most N type B moves) is correct and clean. Part (b) prime-wise gcd-of-valuations invariant, including the zero-tuple convention, is fully correct. Only the survival step is flawed, and it is trivially repairable."}
